name: RHA fillers (Teoxane)

lead: RHA fillers are Teoxane's hyaluronic acid gels, sold as Teosyal RHA outside the US and RHA Redensity in the US. They are designed to flex with facial expression, so people use them around the mouth and lips and in under-eye hollows for smoother lines and a filled look that moves naturally.

A cross-linked HA gel that keeps long HA chains adds soft volume and stretches with movement, then degrades gradually. A 52-week randomized study reported benefit for dynamic perioral lines, and trials have studied under-eye hollows, lips and nasolabial folds.

paras: A licensed clinician injects the area in an office visit and the filled look is visible immediately. People repeat treatments as the gel absorbs, and it can be dissolved with hyaluronidase.
Reported effects include swelling and bruising, and a case report describes hypersensitivity. It is a prescription medical device, results are temporary, and community discussion is thin.

chain: Flexible HA gel moves with face
angle.text: RHA fillers are designed to stay natural in areas that move, so people use them around the mouth and lips and in under-eye hollows. The flexible hyaluronic acid gel fills lines and hollows with a look that follows expression. Randomized perioral and under-eye trials support these uses.

lead: RHA (Resilient Hyaluronic Acid) fillers are cross-linked hyaluronic acid (HA) products from the Swiss company Teoxane, marketed as Teosyal RHA outside the US and RHA Redensity in the US. They were developed to hold up in dynamic areas of the face that move with expression, such as around the mouth. [1][2]
Controlled trials report effectiveness of RHA Redensity for dynamic perioral lines, and trials have studied infraorbital hollows, lips and nasolabial folds. [1][3][4][5]
infobox: Gel that stretches with facial movement

paras: The RHA range uses a manufacturing process meant to preserve long HA chains so the gel stays flexible and resilient in motion. [1] Laboratory work has compared injectability of commercial cross-linked HA fillers [6] and compared cross-linking technologies. [7] Technique articles describe midface volumization with RHA gels. [2]
A case report describes a hypersensitivity reaction to an RHA filler. [8] A multidose hyaluronidase study examined degradation of RHA fillers in vitro. [9]

A 52-week randomized, evaluator-blinded, no-treatment-controlled study evaluated RHA Redensity for moderate-to-severe dynamic perioral rhytides. [1] A prospective registry reported one-year effectiveness and safety of HA fillers in routine practice, and a real-world periorbital study has been published. [10][11] A retrospective study used ultrasound to assess skin density after treatment with an HA-based hydrogel. [12]

Registered trials include perioral rhytids (n=202), infraorbital hollows (n=248; China study recruiting), lips versus Restylane-L (n=202) and nasolabial folds against Juvéderm Ultra XC (n=148) and Perlane-L (n=140). [3][4][5][13][14]
